title: New Year and North Pole
statementMd:
In this problem we assume the Earth to be a completely round ball and its surface a perfect sphere. The length of the equator and any meridian is considered to be exactly $40 000$ kilometers. Thus, travelling from North Pole to South Pole or vice versa takes exactly $20 000$ kilometers.

Limak, a polar bear, lives on the North Pole. Close to the New Year, he helps somebody with delivering packages all around the world. Instead of coordinates of places to visit, Limak got a description how he should move, assuming that he starts from the North Pole. The description consists of $*n*$ parts. In the $*i*$-th part of his journey, Limak should move $*t*_{*i*}$ kilometers in the direction represented by a string $*dir*_{*i*}$ that is one of: "`North`", "`South`", "`West`", "`East`".

Limak isn’t sure whether the description is valid. You must help him to check the following conditions:

- If at any moment of time (before any of the instructions or while performing one of them) Limak is on the North Pole, he can move only to the South.
- If at any moment of time (before any of the instructions or while performing one of them) Limak is on the South Pole, he can move only to the North.
- The journey must end on the North Pole.

Check if the above conditions are satisfied and print "`YES`" or "`NO`" on a single line.

## Input

The first line of the input contains a single integer $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 50$).

The $*i*$-th of next $*n*$ lines contains an integer $*t*_{*i*}$ and a string $*dir*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *t*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$, ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cf8071d3b962bd7ac7bb77393d8cb0cc045dddb1.png)) — the length and the direction of the $*i*$-th part of the journey, according to the description Limak got.

## Output

Print "`YES`" if the description satisfies the three conditions, otherwise print "`NO`", both without the quotes.

## Note

Drawings below show how Limak's journey would look like in first two samples. In the second sample the answer is "`NO`" because he doesn't end on the North Pole.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82aeb8679ccf80c9c32a555b44bfd640c64f9cc4.png)
statementZhMd:
在本题中，我们假设地球是一个完全规则的球体，其表面是一个完美的球面。赤道和任意一条经线的长度都被认为恰好是 $40 000$ 千米。因此，从北极到南极或反向移动恰好需要 $20 000$ 千米。

北极熊 Limak 住在北极。临近新年时，他帮助某人向世界各地运送包裹。Limak 没有得到要访问地点的坐标，而是得到了一份移动说明，并且假设他从北极出发。这份说明由 $*n*$ 个部分组成。在他的旅程的第 $*i*$ 部分中，Limak 应沿着由字符串 $*dir*_{*i*}$ 表示的方向移动 $*t*_{*i*}$ 千米，其中方向字符串是以下之一："`North`"、"`South`"、"`West`"、"`East`"。

Limak 不确定这份说明是否有效。请你帮助他检查以下条件：

- 如果在任意时刻（在执行任何指令之前或执行某条指令的过程中）Limak 位于北极，那么他只能向南移动。
- 如果在任意时刻（在执行任何指令之前或执行某条指令的过程中）Limak 位于南极，那么他只能向北移动。
- 旅程必须在北极结束。

请检查上述条件是否全部满足，并在一行中输出 "`YES`" 或 "`NO`"。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 50$）。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行中，第 $*i*$ 行包含一个整数 $*t*_{*i*}$ 和一个字符串 $*dir*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *t*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$，![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cf8071d3b962bd7ac7bb77393d8cb0cc045dddb1.png)）——根据 Limak 得到的说明，第 $*i*$ 部分旅程的长度和方向。

## 输出格式

如果这份说明满足上述三个条件，则输出 "`YES`"，否则输出 "`NO`"，均不包含引号。

## 说明

下面的图展示了前两个样例中 Limak 的旅程。在第二个样例中，答案是 "`NO`"，因为他没有在北极结束。
